title: Completeness of the 3-SAT to clique reduction
statement: Let $f$ be a 3-CNF formula consisting of $m$ clauses, and let its conflict graph be the simple graph on the vertices $\langle c, \ell\rangle$ (clause index $c$, literal position $\ell$) in which two vertices are adjacent exactly when they belong to different clauses and their literals do not conflict. If $f$ is satisfiable, then this conflict graph has an $m$-clique.
hypotheses_covered: f is a 3-CNF formula with m = f.length clauses
f is satisfiable (there is an assignment satisfying every clause)
replaced:
If a 3-CNF formula $f$ with $m$ clauses is satisfiable, then the conflict graph
$\mathtt{toCliqueGraph}\,f$ contains an $m$-clique: $\mathtt{is3Satisfiable}\,f \to
\mathtt{hasClique}\,(\mathtt{toCliqueGraph}\,f)\,f.\mathtt{length}$.
